issues.description: Identifier naming inconsistency for the quantity getter in StockIngredient: the template implementation (src/de/tum/cit/ase/StockIngredient.java) defines a method named retrieveQuantity(), whereas the rest of the template code (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java and src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java) and the provided solution (solution/src/de/tum/cit/ase/StockIngredient.java) use the conventional getter name getQuantity(). The problem statement also instructs students to "add getters for all the private fields" which implies standard getter names. This mismatch causes compilation errors because Stock.add/take and code in Main call getQuantity(), which does not exist in the template, blocking students from building and running the project.
issues.suggestedFix: Provide a standard getter named getQuantity() in the template StockIngredient class. Either rename the existing retrieveQuantity() method to getQuantity(), or add a public int getQuantity() { return this.quantity; } that delegates to the existing logic. This aligns the template with the problem statement and the rest of the code (Stock and Main) and will restore compilation. Prefer renaming/adding getQuantity() so student code and tests match conventional getter naming.
